option_relations.rationale: Lymphangioma is a type of benign vascular tumor, but it specifically involves lymphatic vessels, whereas hemangioma involves blood vessels. While both are vascular malformations, they are distinct entities. The option is a supertype of the leaf, but the leaf is not a subtype of the option.
Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma (Dabska tumor) is a rare, low-grade malignant vascular tumor, distinct from a benign hemangioma.
Benign lymphangioendothelioma (BLAE) is a rare benign vascular tumor of lymphatic origin, distinct from a hemangioma which is of blood vessel origin.
Pseudo-Kaposi’s sarcoma (acroangiodermatitis) is a reactive vascular proliferation, not a true neoplastic hemangioma.
